cases.title: GPT-written diff with a missed concurrency guard
cases.intent: Add JobStore.claim_next and a drain helper so that four worker threads can drain one JobStore. Each job must be claimed by exactly one worker. Handler errors are out of scope: handlers are trusted not to raise.
cases.evidence: The current folder holds the repository after the change. Check results: the 3 tests in tests/test_store.py pass.

real_problems.text: demo_jobs/store.py, JobStore.claim_next reads and updates self._jobs and the job state without holding self._lock, although add, complete and count hold it. Two worker threads can both see the same pending job and both claim it, so the job is handled twice and the exactly-one-worker requirement fails; iterating _jobs while add() mutates it can also raise RuntimeError.

accepted_related: No test starts concurrent claimers and asserts that each job is claimed once, so the drain test cannot catch the missing lock.

cases.title: GPT-written diff that breaks a public contract
cases.intent: Refactor demo_export.report by moving CSV rendering into a helper. The public behavior of export_report must not change; docs/api.txt is its contract and no documentation change is part of this change.
cases.evidence: The current folder holds the repository after the change. Check results: the 3 tests in tests/test_report.py pass.

real_problems.text: demo_export/report.py, export_report now returns bytes instead of str. docs/api.txt documents a str result that callers may write to a text stream, and demo_export/cli.py passes the result to sys.stdout.write, which raises TypeError, so the public contract and its in-repository consumer break.

accepted_related: The changed test no longer asserts the str result of export_report, so the suite does not catch the break.
docs/api.txt still says str and was not updated.

cases.title: Issue body whose Proposal contradicts its acceptance criteria
cases.intent: An agent must be able to implement this issue without asking questions. The owning file is demo_notify/sender.py.
cases.evidence: The current folder holds demo_notify/sender.py, the file that the issue describes.

real_problems.text: Proposal items 1 to 3 limit a delivery to 3 retries at a fixed 10 second wait and mark the event failed afterwards, while acceptance criterion 2 requires retries without a limit and a wait that doubles each time. An implementer cannot satisfy both.

cases.title: Idempotency design with process-local state in a replicated service

real_problems.text: Design steps 1 to 4 keep the seen event ids in a per-process in-memory set, while the Context says demo-pay runs 3 replicas behind a round-robin balancer and a retry may reach another replica. A duplicate delivered to a different replica (or after a restart, or after eviction from the 100000-id set) is not recognized, so the account is credited twice and the exactly-once goal fails. The dedup state must be shared and durable, for example a unique constraint on event_id in the same database transaction.

accepted_related: The only test sends the duplicate to one handler instance, so it cannot catch the cross-replica duplicate.
Checking the set before the transaction and adding after it is not atomic, so two concurrent deliveries can both pass the check.

cases.title: Rate-limit design that loads limits once against a 60 second change requirement

real_problems.text: Design step 1 reads every limit once at process start into LIMITS and nothing refreshes it, so requirement R2 (a changed limit applies within 60 seconds without a restart) fails; a tenant created later also falls to the default of step 4 until restart. The design needs a periodic refresh or a change subscription.

accepted_related: The only test builds LIMITS by hand and never changes a limit, so it cannot catch the R2 failure.
